findings.eff_zero_variance: Eff is 0.00 on all 10 seeds, with direct_failures and synthetic_failures both 0 everywhere; the training objective is fully satisfied in every run.
findings.ppl_at_base: 10-seed PPL mean 10.894 sits slightly below the base 10.94, i.e. indistinguishable from base.
findings.seed1_is_a_bad_draw: Seed 1, reported alone in earlier single-seed revisions, is among the worst draws on both open metrics (Gen 5.00, PPL 11.250). The single-seed headline understated Gen and overstated PPL cost.
findings.spe_is_bimodal: Spe splits into two clusters with nothing between them - low: seeds 2/3/7/9/10 at 6.32-9.49; high: seeds 1/6/8/4/5 at 11.35-12.35. No seed lands near the 9.709 mean, so the 2.320 SD hides a discrete cause rather than describing a spread.
findings.spe_mechanism: Same cause as the Spe break at --train-margin 10: with full token coverage the edit includes common subject tokens, which neighborhood prompts do contain. Whether a seed's 50-record draw includes subjects made of common tokens determines its cluster.
findings.spe_check: Testable from training-visible data only - correlate each seed's Spe against the corpus frequency of its edited rows (subject_row_selection[].kept_token_frequencies in stage1_config.json), with no reference to held-out prompts.
findings.proposed_fix: --row-norm-cap with --row-norm-cap-frequency-alpha (added in 178f637) caps exactly those rows. Seed 2 is the natural test case at Spe 6.32.
